title: Keep the caller's editor across sudo for vipw and vigr
head: dcaebc8cf8f7
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Preserved EDITOR launches the root user's configured editor, not the caller's selected Omarchy editor
leads.consequence: The default EDITOR names a wrapper, not the selected editor. sudo does not preserve HOME under the stock policy, so a user who selected helix (or vim/code/etc.) in ~/.local/state/omarchy/defaults/editor gets nvim from root's empty defaults/editor when running sudo vipw/vigr. The advertised caller-editor preference is lost even though EDITOR itself is kept. An explicit EDITOR=helix override is a different case. Keep a safe, supported way to convey the caller's actual selection or document the nvim fallback rather than claiming to keep the caller's selected editor.
leads.triage: not_published; root uses HOME=/root so caller's saved editor choice is not used (nvim); Opus report covers this as intended/security-neutral; PR states nvim opens; not a defect

leads.summary: Integrating with current quattro makes the PR's new fixture and an existing fixture fail
leads.consequence: The PR was written before quattro added '--' between editor and file operands. A clean three-way merge retains that delimiter, so the new stub prints 'inline -- /etc/group' where this test requires 'inline /etc/group' (the window assertion similarly expects no '--'). The kept quadruple command-operand-boundaries test also expects omarchy-launch-tui for no-flag calls in a displayless test; the PR now calls nvim inline, so that existing test fails. The current-base test suite cannot pass as written even though the head-only test passes. Update the new fixture for the delimiter and reconcile the prior window-mode fixture with intentional no-Wayland behavior.
leads.triage: corroborated; = Opus F1 (tests fail after rebase); visible

leads.summary: Open #9503's launcher mode bypasses the new no-Wayland inline override
leads.consequence: #9503 changes the terminal-editor switch from inline to mode=windowed/inline/sudo. A direct merge of its launcher into this head has both mode=windowed for a no-flag call and the new 'inline=true' assignment when Wayland is missing, but the terminal branch checks mode, not inline. Thus the combined root vipw path attempts omarchy-launch-tui instead of inline nvim, and the PR's own no-Wayland fixture fails with 'window nvim /etc/group'. Resolve by updating the new override to set the mode variable if #9503 lands, rather than assuming a textually clean merge means a working combined fix. #9503 is diverged, not a stacked dependency; GitHub currently marks that other PR CONFLICTING against its base even though these particular files merge without markers.
leads.triage: confirmed_published; #9503 merge leaves inline fallback dead; Opus followup-1 Q2 reproduced; Details optional note

leads.summary: The no-Wayland inline fallback is ignored for GUI editor selections
leads.consequence: The new branch sets inline=true when WAYLAND_DISPLAY is unset, but the GUI *) branch never checks inline. For a caller whose saved default is code, cursor, zeditor, sublime_text, emacs, or another installed GUI editor, EDITOR=omarchy-launch-editor --inline over SSH/TTY still launches setsid uwsm-app and tries to open a GUI with no display. The newly advertised SSH fallback works for terminal editors only; for GUI choices it inherits an existing failure. If sessionless editing is part of the fix, provide a CLI fallback for this branch or explicitly limit the claim and add a GUI-default fixture.
leads.triage: not_published; GUI editor branch ignores inline; unchanged existing behaviour; under sudo HOME=/root selects nvim; not a regression

leads.summary: The claimed missing /usr/bin/vi fallback contradicts the pinned base package list
leads.consequence: Both the merge base and reviewed head already list vi as a base package, and current quattro still lists it. Omarchy's vi package builds original ex/vi and its Makefile installs /usr/bin/vi. On installs following that package manifest, bare sudo vipw/vigr already have an executable fallback, contrary to the new drop-in's comments, test comment and PR problem statement. Preserving the caller's EDITOR may still improve preference, but it is not needed to avoid the asserted missing-binary failure on this pinned base. Reconcile the motivation and test with the shipped package before claiming stock installs cannot run vipw/vigr.
leads.triage: confirmed_published; vi in base packages + migration 1788596255 (#10307); coordinator verified package list, migration, release tags v4.0.3/v4.0.4 lack it; Opus followup-1 Q1 reproduced bare vigr with published vi package; visible finding 2

leads.summary: New launcher test passes when saved editor selection is completely ignored
leads.consequence: All three launcher assertions use an empty synthetic HOME and only an nvim stub. The stub for omarchy-cmd-present always returns success, unlike the real helper, and no test writes defaults/editor. A plausible regression replacing the launcher's selection-reading block with editor=nvim passes the test verbatim, while users selecting helix or a GUI editor lose their preference. Add a second home with a selected, stubbed nondefault editor and check the final exec target (and a missing-command fallback), not just the default branch.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** Two tests fail after rebasing onto `quattro`, which already ships `/usr/bin/vi`.

### Tests fail after rebasing

`quattro` now passes `--` to the editor (#11495), so `vipw-editor-test.sh` gets `inline -- /etc/group`. The new fallback also makes `command-operand-boundaries-test.sh` fail when `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` is unset.

**Suggested change:** Expect `--` in the new assertions; in the boundaries test, set `WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-1` on the non-inline terminal call.

<details><summary>Reproducer and test fix (fails on quattro 8b4eae6 + dcaebc8)</summary>

# Reproducer: two tests fail once the PR is merged into current quattro

Revisions: PR head `dcaebc8cf8f755dca473758414bc9ef6669a41e2` merged into quattro `8b4eae66da2938ba9559f103b18dbf85cdf28a70`. The merge has no conflicts. Quattro changed `bin/omarchy-launch-editor` after this PR's base: it now passes `--` before the file operands (`exec "$editor" -- "$@"`, `exec omarchy-launch-tui "$editor" -- "$@"`), and `test/shell.d/command-operand-boundaries-test.sh` calls the script without `--inline` and without setting `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`.

```bash
git fetch https://github.com/omacom/omarchy.git quattro pull/11461/head
git checkout --detach 8b4eae66da2938ba9559f103b18dbf85cdf28a70
git merge --no-edit dcaebc8cf8f755dca473758414bc9ef6669a41e2

# Run the way a headless machine, SSH session or CI sandbox would: no WAYLAND_DISPLAY.
env -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY bash test/shell.d/vipw-editor-test.sh; echo "exit $?"
env -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY bash test/shell.d/command-operand-boundaries-test.sh; echo "exit $?"
```

The output below was captured on a tree equal to that merge: the quattro tip plus the PR diff, which `git apply` takes cleanly; a three-way `git merge-file` of the only file both sides touch (`bin/omarchy-launch-editor`) gives the identical result.

Actual output of `test/shell.d/vipw-editor-test.sh` (stdout, then stderr; the `visudo: /etc/sudo.conf is owned by uid 65534` line comes from the review sandbox's user namespace and does not appear on a normal machine):

```
ok - vipw sudoers rule keeps EDITOR for vipw and vigr
```
```
visudo: /etc/sudo.conf is owned by uid 65534, should be 0
got: inline -- /etc/group
not ok - launch-editor edits inline when there is no Wayland session
```
Exit status 1. The same assertion fails with `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` set, because the mismatch is the `--` that quattro now inserts.

Actual output of `test/shell.d/command-operand-boundaries-test.sh` (stdout, then stderr):

```
ok - cmd-present treats an option-shaped command name literally
ok - cmd-missing treats an option-shaped command name literally
ok - cmd-present still finds an ordinary command
ok - pkg-present treats an option-shaped package name literally
ok - pkg-missing treats an option-shaped package name literally
ok - pkg-present still finds an installed package
ok - pkg-add keeps option-shaped package names out of pacman option parsing
ok - pkg-aur-add keeps option-shaped package names out of package-manager option parsing
ok - hw-match treats an option-shaped hardware pattern literally
ok - hw-match still accepts an ordinary hardware pattern
ok - restart-app treats the application name as one literal pkill pattern
ok - launch-editor separates an option-shaped path from editor options
```
```
<-->
<-cquit>
not ok - launch-editor separates a terminal editor path from editor options
```
Exit status 1. The test expected the `omarchy-launch-tui` stub to receive `<nvim> <--> <-cquit>`; with the PR's change and no `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`, the script took the inline path and called the `nvim` stub directly. The same file passes on quattro without the PR (no `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`), and passes on the merge when `WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-1` is set.

Fix that makes both pass on the merge with `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` unset (checked in the same sandbox):

```diff
--- a/test/shell.d/vipw-editor-test.sh
+++ b/test/shell.d/vipw-editor-test.sh
@@
 result=$(WAYLAND_DISPLAY= launch /etc/group)
-[[ $result == "inline /etc/group" ]] ||
+[[ $result == "inline -- /etc/group" ]] ||
   fail "launch-editor edits inline when there is no Wayland session" "got: $result"
 
 result=$(WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-1 launch /etc/group)
-[[ $result == "window nvim /etc/group" ]] ||
+[[ $result == "window nvim -- /etc/group" ]] ||
   fail "launch-editor still opens a window inside a session" "got: $result"
 
 result=$(WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-1 launch --inline /etc/group)
-[[ $result == "inline /etc/group" ]] ||
+[[ $result == "inline -- /etc/group" ]] ||
   fail "launch-editor still honors --inline inside a session" "got: $result"
--- a/test/shell.d/command-operand-boundaries-test.sh
+++ b/test/shell.d/command-operand-boundaries-test.sh
@@
-HOME="$fake_home" PATH="$mock_bin:$ROOT/bin:$PATH" OMARCHY_TEST_EDITOR_CALLS="$editor_calls" \
+WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-1 HOME="$fake_home" PATH="$mock_bin:$ROOT/bin:$PATH" OMARCHY_TEST_EDITOR_CALLS="$editor_calls" \
   "$ROOT/bin/omarchy-launch-editor" -cquit
```
(The second hunk is the non-inline terminal-editor call, the one followed by the `<nvim>\n<-->\n<-cquit>` assertion.)

</details>

### `/usr/bin/vi` already ships on quattro

#10307 added the original ex/vi (`/usr/bin/vi -> ex`) to the base packages plus a migration (in this PR's base, not v4.0.3/v4.0.4). With it installed, `vigr` without the PR opens that vi and saves, so the "Omarchy does not ship" comments are inaccurate.

**Suggested change:** Describe the drop-in as keeping the caller's editor (as for visudo), not fixing a missing `vi`.

<details><summary>Reproducer (vigr with the vi package, without this PR)</summary>

# Reproducer: bare `vigr` with Omarchy's `vi` package opens the original vi and saves

On the PR's base branch, `install/omarchy-base.packages` lists `vi`, and `migrations/1788596255.sh` (`omarchy-pkg-add vi`, from #10307) installs it on existing machines. The package is in the stable, rc and edge repositories with sha256 `a1ff749060b4cc7094d99166507afe96e9578e504a562ce7553e1c039ad00d95` (the value in all three repository databases). This runs util-linux `vigr` as uid 0 in an unprivileged user namespace, with that package's `/usr/bin/vi -> ex`, `EDITOR` unset (what sudo's env_reset leaves without the PR's drop-in), a throwaway `/etc`, and a pty from `script`. It does not use sudo and changes nothing outside a `mktemp -d` directory.

Fetch the package:

```bash
curl -fLo 'vi-1:070224-9-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst' 'https://pkgs.omarchy.org/stable/x86_64/vi-1:070224-9-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst'
echo 'a1ff749060b4cc7094d99166507afe96e9578e504a562ce7553e1c039ad00d95  vi-1:070224-9-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst' | sha256sum -c
```

Actual output of the check:

```
'vi-1:070224-9-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst': OK
```

Save this as `vigr-with-vi.sh` and run `bash vigr-with-vi.sh 'vi-1:070224-9-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst'`:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Bare vigr (EDITOR unset, as sudo leaves it) with Omarchy's vi package as /usr/bin/vi.
# Runs vigr as uid 0 in an unprivileged user namespace over a throwaway /etc.
# Needs bwrap, util-linux (vigr, script), tar with zstd, GNU sed.
set -u
pkg=${1:?usage: vigr-with-vi.sh path/to/vi-1:070224-9-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst}

work=$(mktemp -d)
mkdir -p "$work/pkg" "$work/etc" "$work/root" "$work/usrbin"
tar --force-local --zstd -xf "$pkg" -C "$work/pkg"
tar --force-local --zstd -tvf "$pkg" | grep 'usr/bin/.'
vigr -V
bwrap --version

printf 'root:x:0:0::/root:/bin/bash\n' >"$work/etc/passwd"
printf 'root:x:0:root\nwheel:x:998:\n' >"$work/etc/group"
cp "$work/etc/group" "$work/group.before"

# Keystrokes: G (last line), o (open a line below), the text, Esc, :wq, Enter.
printf 'Goreview:x:4242:\033:wq\r' >"$work/keys"

# A /usr/bin for the namespace: every host /usr/bin entry as a link into a
# read-only bind of the real one, plus the package's ex and its vi -> ex link.
for f in /usr/bin/*; do ln -s "/hostbin/${f##*/}" "$work/usrbin/${f##*/}"; done
rm -f "$work/usrbin/ex" "$work/usrbin/vi"
cp -a "$work/pkg/usr/bin/ex" "$work/usrbin/ex"
ln -s ex "$work/usrbin/vi"

bwrap --unshare-user --uid 0 --gid 0 \
  --ro-bind /usr /usr \
  --ro-bind /usr/bin /hostbin \
  --ro-bind "$work/usrbin" /usr/bin \
  --symlink usr/bin /bin --symlink usr/bin /sbin \
  --symlink usr/lib /lib --symlink usr/lib /lib64 \
  --bind "$work/etc" /etc --bind "$work/root" /root \
  --ro-bind "$work/keys" /keys \
  --proc /proc --dev /dev --tmpfs /tmp --tmpfs /var --dir /var/tmp --dir /var/lib/ex \
  --clearenv \
  --setenv PATH /usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin \
  --setenv HOME /root --setenv TERM xterm \
  /bin/bash -c 'id -u; ls -l /usr/bin/vi /usr/bin/ex; env | LC_ALL=C sort; (sleep 2; cat /keys; sleep 3) | script -qec "/usr/bin/vigr; echo vigr-exit=\$?" /dev/null' \
  >"$work/transcript.raw" 2>"$work/bwrap.stderr"
echo "bwrap exit: $?"
echo "bwrap stderr bytes: $(wc -c <"$work/bwrap.stderr")"

echo "--- transcript (escape sequences, carriage returns and backspaces removed)"
sed -e 's/\x1b\[[0-9;?]*[A-Za-z]//g' -e 's/\x1b[=>]//g' -e 's/\r//g' -e 's/\x08//g' "$work/transcript.raw"
echo
echo "--- postconditions"
echo '$ diff "$work/group.before" "$work/etc/group"'
diff "$work/group.before" "$work/etc/group"
echo '$ ls -a "$work/etc"'
ls -a "$work/etc"
echo '$ cat "$work/etc/group-"'
cat "$work/etc/group-"
```

Actual output (stdout; stderr was empty, exit status 0). The transcript section is printed by the script's own `sed`, which removes terminal escape sequences, carriage returns and backspaces; nothing else is removed. `.vipw.vBIiVC` is vigr's random temporary name.


vi opened vigr's temporary copy of `/etc/group` as root, the keystrokes added `review:x:4242:` and `:wq` saved it, and vigr installed it (exit 0) and kept the old file as `/etc/group-`. So without the PR, bare `sudo vigr` on a machine with this package opens the original vi and works. Run on util-linux 2.42.3 and bubblewrap 0.12.0; the keystrokes are sent after fixed 2-second and 3-second delays, so a much slower machine may need longer ones.

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Verified**
- `visudo -cf` parses the drop-in, alone and included from an Arch-configured `/etc/sudoers` rendered from sudo's template with all Omarchy drop-ins; `cvtsudoers` binds `env_keep += EDITOR` to exactly `/usr/bin/vipw` and `/usr/bin/vigr`.
- util-linux `vipw.c` (v2.42.4) reads only `EDITOR`, keeps its first word and falls back to `/usr/bin/vi`.
- Real `vigr` run as uid 0 in a namespace with the environment sudo leaves and `EDITOR="omarchy-launch-editor --inline"`: with the PR's script it calls the editor inline (a stand-in nvim) and installs the change.
- The drop-in ships through omarchy-settings (`etc/` copied wholesale, mode 0440); no file list or migration is needed.
- Existing callers that omit `--inline` (config editor, branding, clipboard) start from the Hyprland session and keep the window path.

**Optional notes**
- **#9503** ("Keep the sudo editor on one that blocks") replaces `inline` with `mode`. On their common base the two merge without a conflict (against current `quattro`, #9503 conflicts only in the `exec` block), but this PR's `inline=true` line is then never read, and `vipw-editor-test.sh` fails with `got: window nvim /etc/group`. Whichever lands second should rewrite the fallback in terms of `mode`, for example `[[ -n ${WAYLAND_DISPLAY:-} || $mode != "windowed" ]] || mode="inline"`; #9503's windowed assertions then also need `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` set.
- **#13094 / #13044 / #13305** make the GUI branch block (`--wait`) when `inline` is true. Combined with this PR, a non-inline GUI launch without `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` blocks, and #13094's `non-inline launch passes no wait flag` fails headless. Applying the fallback only in the terminal-editor branch (`if [[ $inline == "true" || -z ${WAYLAND_DISPLAY:-} ]]`) kept these tests passing with #13094 and #13044 (with the rebase test fix; #13305 by reading, as it carries #13044's script).
- `sudo -E vigr` keeps `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` and `HOME`, so it still takes the window path; the change covers plain `sudo vipw`/`sudo vigr` only. Not run.

<details><summary>Reproducer: #9503 merged with this PR</summary>

# Reproducer: #9503 and this PR merge cleanly, and the merge silently disables this PR's fallback

#9503 (head `107e7576a225`) replaces the `inline` boolean in `bin/omarchy-launch-editor` with `mode` (`inline`, `sudo` or `windowed`). This PR adds `[[ -n ${WAYLAND_DISPLAY:-} ]] || inline=true` after the flag parsing. On the common base `31bd80daa461` (both PRs start from the same `bin/omarchy-launch-editor` blob, `8a69dabd4bb`), git merges the two without a conflict:

```bash
git merge-file -L 11461 -L base -L 9503 le.11461 le.base le.9503; echo "conflicts=$?"
# conflicts=0
```

The merged file keeps this PR's line, but nothing reads `$inline` any more:

```bash
case "${1:-}" in
--inline)
  mode="inline"
  shift
  ;;
--sudo)
  mode="sudo"
  shift
  ;;
*)
  mode="windowed"
  ;;
esac

# vipw and vigr keep only the first word of $EDITOR, so --inline never reaches
# here under sudo. Without a Wayland session there is no window to open anyway.
[[ -n ${WAYLAND_DISPLAY:-} ]] || inline=true
...
nvim | vim | nano | micro | hx | helix | fresh)
  if [[ $mode == "windowed" ]]; then
    exec omarchy-launch-tui "$editor" "$@"
```

Rebasing #9503 onto quattro with this PR applied conflicts only in the `exec` block (quattro's `--` operands); the `inline=true` line merges outside the conflict either way.

Tree: `31bd80daa461` + #9503's diff + this PR's three files, with that automatic merge for `bin/omarchy-launch-editor`.

```bash
env -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY bash test/shell.d/vipw-editor-test.sh; echo "exit $?"
```

Actual output (stdout, then stderr; the `visudo: /etc/sudo.conf` line comes from the review sandbox's user namespace), exit 1, identical with `WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-1` exported:

```
ok - vipw sudoers rule keeps EDITOR for vipw and vigr
```
```
visudo: /etc/sudo.conf is owned by uid 65534, should be 0
got: window nvim /etc/group
not ok - launch-editor edits inline when there is no Wayland session
```

#9503's own tests pass on the same tree (`launch-editor-sudo-test.sh` prints `ok - --sudo blocks for every editor the chooser offers` and `ok - the windowed and inline paths are unchanged`, exit 0; `editor-env-test.sh` exit 0), so nothing in #9503's suite notices.

End to end with the util-linux `vigr` as uid 0 in a nested namespace, `EDITOR="omarchy-launch-editor --inline"`, `HOME=/root`, no `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`, and a logging stand-in for `omarchy-launch-tui` that fails as a root launch without a session would: the stand-in received `<nvim>` `</etc/.vipw.uSOgx8>`, and vigr printed

```
omarchy-launch-tui stand-in: no session reachable
vigr: omarchy-launch-editor: unsuccessful execution
vigr: /etc/group unchanged
```

with exit 1.

